Prevention: Use less susceptible cowpea varieties (e.g. slipea 1, 2 and 3)
Use correct planting density (wider spacing such as 50 cm x 30 cm or 50 cm x 40 cm)
Intercrop cowpea with maize or sorghum
Remove weeds at 3 and 6 weeks after planting
Plough and harrow to destroy fungal inoculum in the soil
Monitoring: Look for symptoms on leaves, stems, pods and whole plant:
Leaves: brown or rust- coloured circular to angular spots, chlorosis, and abnormal leaf fall
Seeds: poor to no germination, small and abnormal
Whole plant: abnormal growth and development
Direct Control: Remove diseased plants and burn outside the crop field
Remove heavily infected plants to prevent spread of inoculum
Early pruning of infected leaves to prevent further spread of inoculum
Spray aqueous leaf extracts from neem and pepper (leaf powder: 100 g/ litres water)
Restrictions: Apply early in the morning or late in the evening; Do not apply when it is raining or windy; Use protective gears to avoid being poisoned
